headline: The country whose *lowest point* beats Britain's highest

cover.headline: Its *lowest point* is higher than Ben Nevis

intent: Lesotho is the only country lying entirely above 1,000 m; its lowest point, where the Makhaleng meets the Orange River, is 1,400 m up, higher than the summit of Ben Nevis, and the whole kingdom is an island inside South Africa.

post.premise: There is a country where the lowest spot is higher than Britain's highest mountain

youtube.title: The country whose lowest point beats Britain's highest mountain ⛰️
youtube.description:
There is a kingdom in southern Africa where you cannot get below 1,400 metres: its lowest river junction is higher than the summit of Ben Nevis. This map story finds that lowest point, climbs to the highest, and pulls back to show the whole country sealed inside its only neighbour.
Could you live 1.4 km up, minimum? Tell us below.

vo.text: There is a country where you cannot get down to sea level. You cannot even get close.

open.direction: plunge from the southern tip of Africa onto the highlands; the border draws itself on 'country'

vo.text: This is Lesotho. Its lowest point is here, where two rivers meet on the border, and even that is 1,400 metres above the sea.

beats.direction: push to the south-west corner; the lowest-point pin drops in the river junction; counter climbs to 1,400

elements.label: metres above sea level · the lowest spot

vo.text: That is the highest low point of any country on Earth. Ben Nevis, the tallest mountain in Britain, is 1,345 metres. It would not reach the bottom of Lesotho.

beats.direction: a mountain prop pops beside the pin, standing for Ben Nevis; card with both numbers; flash on 'bottom'

card.text: lower than Lesotho's lowest point, 1,400 m

vo.text: From there the land only climbs, up to Thabana Ntlenyana at 3,482 metres. More than 80 percent of the country sits above 1,800 metres. They call it the Kingdom in the Sky.

beats.direction: camera rides a line from the low point north-east to the summit; the peak pin drops; the SKY tag stamps the highlands

vo.text: And it is an island. Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa, one of only three countries on Earth locked inside another.

beats.direction: pull right out; South Africa fills solid around it so the country reads as a hole; border pulses

vo.text: A whole country where the lowest you can go is still higher than Britain's highest mountain.
Follow for a new map story every day.

research.topic: Lesotho is the only independent state lying entirely above 1,000 m; its lowest point, the junction of the Orange (Senqu) and Makhaleng rivers, is 1,400 m, the highest low point of any country, above Ben Nevis (1,345 m); its highest point is Thabana Ntlenyana (3,482 m); over 80% of the country is above 1,800 m; it is entirely enclaved by South Africa, one of three enclaved states with San Marino and Vatican City.

myths.myth: Nepal or Bhutan is the highest country, so it must have the highest low point.
myths.reality: Nepal's lowest point is about 60 m and Bhutan's about 97 m; only Lesotho never drops below 1,000 m.

landscape.our_gap: Lesotho elevation clips are a flag and a list; nobody pins the actual lowest river junction on the satellite map, counts its height, stands Ben Nevis next to it, climbs to the summit, and pulls out to the enclave.
